captions.instagram:
How does the reproductive system work?

Two small sets of organs, deep in the pelvis, can start a whole new person. See the organs as clean diagrams, watch the brain switch on puberty, run the 28-day cycle as a clock, follow one sperm and one egg become a ball of cells, and grow a baby from a lentil to a watermelon.

→ Deep in the pelvis, two almond-sized ovaries hold the eggs, and a pear-sized uterus waits.
→ The testes make about 100 million sperm a day, stored in a coiled tube 6 metres long.
→ Puberty starts in the brain: GnRH wakes the pituitary, which sends LH and FSH to the ovaries or testes.
→ Each month a follicle ripens in the ovary, and an LH surge makes it release one egg.
→ Progesterone thickens the lining; if no baby starts, it is shed as a period, and the clock restarts.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/reproductionclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does the reproductive system work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Two small sets of organs, deep in the pelvis, can start a whole new person. See the organs as clean diagrams, watch the brain switch on puberty, run the 28-day cycle as a clock, follow one sperm and one egg become a ball of cells, and grow a baby from a lentil to a watermelon.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/reproductionclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/reproductionclear

In this video:
• Two sets of organs. Ovaries store eggs and release about one a month into the fallopian tubes, which lead to the uterus.
• Puberty starts in the brain. The hypothalamus starts pulsing GnRH, the pituitary answers with LH and FSH, and the ovaries or testes make oestrogen or testosterone.
• A monthly clock. A cycle lasts 21 to 35 days.
• 23 + 23 = 46. In the fallopian tube, one sperm gets through the egg's coat and the coat hardens behind it.
• Forty weeks. From a lentil with a beating heart at week 6 to about 3 to 3.5 kg at week 40.
• Care and respect. Check-ups keep mothers and babies safe: India's maternal mortality fell from 398 to 88 per 100,000 births between 1997–98 and 2020–22.
